required_facts.statement: Data-informed decision making uses evidence as an input while also considering context and judgment.
source_refs: amplitude_playbook#https://blog.amplitude.com/data-driven-data-informed-data-inspired :: Are You Data-driven, Data-informed or Data-inspired?

required_facts.statement: Data-driven decision making places stronger emphasis on allowing data to determine the choice.
source_refs: amplitude_playbook#https://blog.amplitude.com/data-driven-data-informed-data-inspired :: Are You Data-driven, Data-informed or Data-inspired?

required_facts.statement: Identify the decision and relevant evidence, interpret what the data supports, and consider qualitative context and constraints.
source_refs: amplitude_playbook#https://blog.amplitude.com/data-driven-data-informed-data-inspired :: Are You Data-driven, Data-informed or Data-inspired?

required_facts.statement: Explain the chosen action in terms of the evidence, assumptions, and uncertainties that shaped it.
source_refs: amplitude_playbook#https://blog.amplitude.com/data-driven-data-informed-data-inspired :: Are You Data-driven, Data-informed or Data-inspired?

misconceptions.statement: Available historical data may not capture the opportunity or context of a new direction.
source_refs: amplitude_playbook#https://blog.amplitude.com/data-driven-data-informed-data-inspired :: Are You Data-driven, Data-informed or Data-inspired?

briefs.learning_objective: Use feature flags to control a staged rollout of a change to a subset of users.

required_facts.statement: A feature flag changes whether specified users receive a feature without requiring a new deployment for each exposure change.
Percentage rollout exposes a controlled fraction of eligible users to the feature.
source_refs: amplitude_playbook#https://help.amplitude.com/hc/en-us/articles/360061687311-Working-with-feature-flags-and-feature-rollouts :: Create a feature flag | Amplitude Docs

required_facts.statement: Choose the eligible audience and initial exposure, monitor the result, and expand exposure only after checking readiness.
source_refs: atlassian_agile#https://www.atlassian.com/agile/product-management/product-release :: Product release guide: Key phases and best practices | Atlassian

required_facts.statement: Preserve an explicit rollback option so a problematic change can be turned off or withdrawn.
source_refs: amplitude_playbook#https://help.amplitude.com/docs/en/feature-experiment/workflow/make-decision-experiment :: Make a decision on your experiment | Amplitude Docs

required_facts.statement: Write the rollout as explicit exposure stages with a monitoring check at each stage and a stated metric or quality trigger for turning the feature off.
source_refs: amplitude_playbook#https://help.amplitude.com/hc/en-us/articles/360061687311-Working-with-feature-flags-and-feature-rollouts :: Create a feature flag | Amplitude Docs

misconceptions.statement: A feature flag by itself does not establish that a change caused an improvement.
source_refs: amplitude_playbook#https://help.amplitude.com/hc/en-us/articles/360061687311-Working-with-feature-flags-and-feature-rollouts :: Create a feature flag | Amplitude Docs

briefs.learning_objective: Maintain a holdout group to isolate and measure the long-run incremental impact of a change.

required_facts.statement: A holdout group is a randomly selected subset excluded from a change so it remains a comparison baseline.
Comparing target outcomes for exposed users with the held-out baseline helps estimate the change’s incremental effect over time.
Define the eligible audience, holdout size, excluded changes, comparison metric, and observation period.
Choose the holdout size using both available traffic and the statistical needs of the comparison; Amplitude describes 5–10% as a starting recommendation, not a universal requirement.
Keep assignment and exclusions consistent through the observation period so baseline users do not receive the treatment.

misconceptions.statement: A holdout configured in Amplitude cannot protect users from experiments that were not configured to include that holdout.

briefs.learning_objective: Assess whether a product or feature is ready to launch by checking it against defined readiness dimensions -- support, sales, and monitoring -- before it ships to customers.

required_facts.statement: Launch readiness checks whether the capabilities needed to safely introduce and support the product are in place.
source_refs: atlassian_agile#https://www.atlassian.com/agile/product-management/product-launch-checklist :: How to Launch a Product? Step-by-Step Checklist | Atlassian

required_facts.statement: Readiness includes technical quality, support preparation, sales preparation, monitoring, and operational response.
source_refs: atlassian_agile#https://www.atlassian.com/agile/product-management/product-launch-checklist :: How to Launch a Product? Step-by-Step Checklist | Atlassian

required_facts.statement: Complete each readiness check with evidence, a responsible owner, and an unresolved action for any failed item.
source_refs: atlassian_agile#https://www.atlassian.com/agile/product-management/product-launch-checklist :: How to Launch a Product? Step-by-Step Checklist | Atlassian

required_facts.statement: Use the agreed checklist to recommend proceeding or holding, explicitly identifying any unmet gate and the risk it creates.
source_refs: atlassian_agile#https://www.atlassian.com/agile/product-management/product-release :: Product release guide: Key phases and best practices | Atlassian

briefs.learning_objective: Plan the timing, sequencing, and audience segmentation of internal and external launch communications for a product or feature launch.

required_facts.statement: A communication plan specifies how relevant information will reach the people who need it.
The plan identifies audiences, messages, channels, timing, and responsible communicators.
source_refs: atlassian_agile#https://www.atlassian.com/work-management/project-collaboration/communication-plan :: How to Create a Communication Plan [+ a Template] | The Workstream

required_facts.statement: Build a plan by mapping each audience’s information needs to a message, delivery channel, owner, and cadence.
source_refs: atlassian_agile#https://www.atlassian.com/work-management/project-collaboration/communication-plan :: How to create a communication plan

required_facts.statement: Review whether messages are reaching the intended audience and update the plan when project needs change.
source_refs: atlassian_agile#https://www.atlassian.com/work-management/project-collaboration/communication-plan :: How to create a communication plan

required_facts.statement: For a launch, sequence audience-specific messages before, during, and after introduction and specify the owner and channel for each.
source_refs: atlassian_agile#https://www.atlassian.com/agile/product-management/product-launch-timeline :: Product Launch Timeline: Stages, Checklist, & Tips | Atlassian

briefs.learning_objective: Prepare sales and support teams with the materials and talking points they need to represent a new feature or product to customers without engineering hand-holding.

required_facts.statement: Product enablement prepares customer-facing teams to explain and support a product effectively.
Enablement can include product knowledge, training, documentation, and practical materials for sales and support.
Identify each team’s needs and build an enablement plan with materials, training sessions, owners, and completion timing.
source_refs: atlassian_agile#https://www.atlassian.com/agile/product-management/product-launch-checklist :: How to Launch a Product? Step-by-Step Checklist | Atlassian

required_facts.statement: Check that customer-facing teams can explain the product’s value and handle common questions before broad introduction.
source_refs: atlassian_agile#https://www.atlassian.com/agile/product-management/product-launch-checklist :: How to Launch a Product? Step-by-Step Checklist | Atlassian

required_facts.statement: Prepare an enablement packet with the feature’s value, talking points, frequently asked questions, known limitations, and an escalation route.
source_refs: atlassian_agile#https://www.atlassian.com/agile/product-management/product-launch-checklist :: How to Launch a Product? Step-by-Step Checklist | Atlassian

briefs.learning_objective: Partner effectively with designers throughout the product development process, from ideation to handoff.

required_facts.statement: Design collaboration combines understanding of user needs with design and technical perspectives.
The shared discussion should focus on the user problem and product goals rather than personal preferences.
Prepare a design discussion with the problem, relevant research, goals, and constraints.
Invite design alternatives, evaluate them against the shared criteria, and record questions and next steps.
The PM contributes the user problem, goals, and product constraints; designers contribute design alternatives and rationale, with review checkpoints agreed across the partnership.

misconceptions.statement: Product critique is not an attack on the person who created the design.

briefs.learning_objective: Map a user's end-to-end journey through a product to identify friction points and opportunities.

required_facts.statement: A journey map visualizes the process a person goes through to accomplish a goal.
A journey map specifies an actor, scenario, phases, actions, thoughts, emotions, and opportunities.
Choose the actor and scenario, map the phases and actions, and add research-grounded thoughts and emotions.
Use the mapped experience to identify pain points and opportunities for improvement.

misconceptions.statement: A journey map should not be presented as research evidence when its contents are only assumptions.

briefs.learning_objective: Give actionable, objective-anchored feedback on wireframes and prototypes.

required_facts.statement: Constructive design feedback describes an observable issue and relates it to the intended user outcome.
Separate an observation from its interpretation so the recipient can understand and discuss the concern.
source_refs: pichler_blog#https://www.romanpichler.com/blog/offering-constructive-feedback-a-framework-for-product-people/ :: A Framework for Offering Feedback in Product Management

required_facts.statement: Give feedback by describing what you observed, explaining its effect or concern, and making a clear, actionable request.
source_refs: pichler_blog#https://www.romanpichler.com/blog/offering-constructive-feedback-a-framework-for-product-people/ :: A Framework for Offering Feedback in Product Management

required_facts.statement: Invite the other person’s perspective and discuss whether the requested change addresses the shared goal.
source_refs: pichler_blog#https://www.romanpichler.com/blog/offering-constructive-feedback-a-framework-for-product-people/ :: A Framework for Offering Feedback in Product Management

misconceptions.statement: Judgments about a person’s intentions or character are not the same as observations of their work.
source_refs: pichler_blog#https://www.romanpichler.com/blog/offering-constructive-feedback-a-framework-for-product-people/ :: A Framework for Offering Feedback in Product Management

briefs.learning_objective: Translate usability test findings into concrete design decisions.

required_facts.statement: Synthesis connects observed usability problems to design changes rather than merely forwarding session notes.
Interpret observations alongside recruitment, task design, facilitation, and other data before treating them as reliable findings.
source_refs: nngroup_articles#https://www.nngroup.com/articles/usability-data-in-analysis/?lm=affinity-diagram&pt=article :: 6 Dimensions for Assessing Usability Data in Analysis - NN/G

required_facts.statement: Look for repeated and consistent evidence and distinguish a real pattern from an isolated or confounded observation.
source_refs: nngroup_articles#https://www.nngroup.com/articles/usability-data-in-analysis/?lm=affinity-diagram&pt=article :: 6 Dimensions for Assessing Usability Data in Analysis - NN/G

required_facts.statement: Rank findings by their consequence for the user’s goal and strength of supporting evidence, then propose specific changes connected to the highest-priority findings.
source_refs: nngroup_articles#https://www.nngroup.com/articles/usability-data-in-analysis/?lm=affinity-diagram&pt=article :: 6 Dimensions for Assessing Usability Data in Analysis - NN/G

required_facts.statement: Discuss the proposed changes with design and retain the supporting findings so later decisions can be checked against the original evidence.
